children: Royal Caribbean is breaking into the resort business, striking a $3 billion deal to acquire a 50% stake in the parent company of Sandals and Beaches Resorts.
Royal Caribbean, the world's largest cruise company by market value, expects the deal to boost earnings next year. The companies anticipate the deal to close in early 2027.

The partnership, structured as a joint venture, would operate the Sandals and Beaches all-inclusive resorts in the Caribbean. A board including Royal Caribbean Chief Executive Jason Liberty and Sandals Executive Chairman Adam Stewart would oversee the venture, with Stewart maintaining a leadership position. The companies said they plan to keep the existing Sandals and Beaches brands.

The partnership aims to grow Royal Caribbean's participation in the global vacation market, as well as accelerate the expansion of Sandals and Beaches Resorts, the companies said. Initially, the joint venture would comprise 18 properties across the two brands, including adults-only Sandals and family-oriented Beaches, spread throughout the Caribbean with additional properties under development.
The companies additionally aim to connect their loyalty programs, incentivizing people to stay within their ecosystems when planning vacation.

The deal comes after Sandals hired bankers to explore a sale last year, The Wall Street Journal first reported. A previous effort to sell the privately held company stalled out when the Covid-19 pandemic began, people familiar with those talks said.
Royal Caribbean shares were up 1.7% to $238.84 in premarket trading.
